title: Canonical compact-support realization factorization interface
statement:
Fix a universe $u$, a prime $\ell$, and a field $k:\mathrm{Type}\,u$ of positive prime characteristic different from $\ell$. Use separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], compactifications $c=(X\xrightarrow{j}Z\xrightarrow{g}Y)$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], and finite normed coefficient extensions $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in the same universe [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Use the completed integral categories [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], their strict reduction $\mathcal R$, total limit $\mathcal L$ and adjunction unit $u$ [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], the actual simultaneous operations $o$ [def-sf-integral-system-operations], and their realization model $m$ and canonical bridge $b$ [def-sf-integral-system-canonical-bridge]. Use the fixed proper/open scalar mates, lattice comparisons and system-presentation isomorphism of [def-pur-compact-support-realization-coordinates], and the completed coefficient presentation $H_X$ of [def-pur-completed-coefficient-presentation-transport]. For an integral object $K$, define $\rho$ to be systemComparison followed by systemPresentation at $\mathcal R K$. For an integral reconstruction model $M$ of [lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization], define $q_K$ to be the actual reduction/limit unit on $P^0_R H_XK$, followed by $\mathcal L(\rho_{H_XK})$, followed by the inverse of that parent's limitPresentation. Here $P^0_R=Rg_{*,R}j_{!,R}$. For scalar-realization data $A_X,A_Z,A_Y$ [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization], define realizedFactorization at $K$ as the ordered composite: inverse target lattice comparison; realization of inverseOrZero$(q_K)$ [def-zl-integral-generator-admissibility-inverse]; properRealization at $j_{!,R}H_XK$; proper image of openRealization at $H_XK$; and compact-support image of the source lattice comparison.

For a comparison family $C$ of [lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization] and an equality $h:C_E.\mathrm{reduction}=\mathcal R_E$, define atNormalized by transporting only that reduction presentation along $h$, retaining all components of $C_E$ at $c$. Define $\operatorname{IsFactorized}(C)$ to mean the following predicate, not an existence assertion for $C$. For every finite normed extension $F/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\mathrm{Type}\,u$, there is such an equality $h$ for $C_F$; there are operations $o$ with a realization model and canonical bridge; and for every choice of $o,m,b$, every pair $X,Y$ of the given $k$-schemes, every $k$-morphism $f:X\to Y$, every compactification $c$ of $f$, every scalar-realization datum $A_Z$ on its intermediate scheme, and every completed bounded constructible integral $K$ on $X$, the following hold in the whole indicated derived categories: $q_K$ is invertible; $\mathcal R(q_K)$ followed by the parent's $\alpha_K$ equals $\rho_{H_XK}$; properRealization at $j_{!,R}H_XK$ is invertible; openRealizationInverse at $H_XK$ is invertible; and the realization component of atNormalized at the rationalized lattice $K$ equals the specified realizedFactorization, using the source and target scalar data of $C_F$. No Tor-window restriction or algebraic closure of $k$ is imposed.
